controlling_quote: Ensure each logo is displayed at an appropriate size, uses its approved color format, and is not distorted or altered in any way.
note: The official pack ships black and white artwork only — there is no grey variant, so a neutral-grey rendering is not an approved color format. OpenAI separately distinguishes permitted from prohibited relationship language: 'building on' is allowed, 'building with' is not.

controlling_quote: No alterations of our trademarks (changes to color, font, proportion, or otherwise) are permitted.
note: The strictest of the sixteen on two counts: it names colour changes explicitly, and it requires prior approval of the materials themselves — 'You may only use our trademarks as specifically permitted by us and only in materials we approve beforehand.' An official one-colour Claude asset does ship in the press kit, but it is white; rendering it grey is still a colour change under the quoted rule.

controlling_quote: Don't combine your logo with the Google G or modify the Google G in any way, including changing the color.
note: Google treats compatibility signalling as affirmatively permission-gated: showing compatibility with Google products is listed among the cases where permission must be requested through Partner Marketing Hub. Gemini-specific guidelines exist but sit behind an approved-partner login and could not be read, so this record rests on Google's general rules, which the specific ones are more likely to tighten than loosen. Note also that support.gemini.com is the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange, a different company — not a source for this record.

controlling_quote: We may grant others the right to use our Marks, but you are not permitted to.
note: Silent on colour specifically, but the blanket rule reaches it: 'only use our logos exactly as provided at the download link below, without any alteration or adjustment.' The asset archive returns HTTP 403 and its contents could not be confirmed. The page identifies the trademark owner as 'SpaceXAI' rather than 'xAI' — flagged, not relied upon.

controlling_quote: The name "ElevenLabs" and our logos, product or service names, slogans, and the look and feel of the Services are trademarks of ElevenLabs and may not be copied, imitated or used, in whole or in part, without our prior written permission.
note: The brand page itself publishes no restriction on artwork — its only 'what to avoid' list concerns spelling the name. The binding clause is in the Terms of Use, which makes the colour question moot: any unlicensed use requires permission regardless of treatment.

controlling_quote: Without the prior written consent of Retell AI, you are not permitted to make use of any of its Marks.
note: The public /logos page is download buttons and nothing else — no usage rule, no colour rule, no clear-space rule, no linked guidelines document. A freely downloadable asset is not a grant, and here the governing clause sits in the Terms of Service instead.

controlling_quote: Do not alter these files, imply a relationship, affiliation, or endorsement by Vapi of your product, service, or business.
note: One of only two providers of the sixteen that addresses compatibility-style implication directly, and it prohibits it. The approved monochrome pairing is ink on cream, not grey, so a neutral-grey silhouette fails on the palette as well as on the no-alteration rule.

controlling_quote: All Materials are the copyrighted property of Bland AI or its subsidiaries or affiliates under the laws of the United States and other countries. Bland AI reserves all rights not expressly granted in these Terms.
note: Publishes no brand, press, or trademark page at all — every candidate path returns 404 and no such link appears anywhere in the site navigation. An SVG exists as an undocumented site asset, which is not a published download. This is the highest-uncertainty record of the sixteen: nothing is prohibited on its face and nothing is granted, and rights are expressly reserved.

controlling_quote: Synthflow Logo — Always use the logo as provided. Maintain clear space around the mark, ensure high contrast against backgrounds, with no alterations.
note: The brand guide governs rendering but publishes no general third-party grant; its permission clause sits inside a reselling section and is scoped to resellers, so it is not read as a universal requirement here. Recolouring is barred twice over: 'no alterations' and 'Always use official color values... avoid applying tints, gradients, or unapproved variations.' Assets are distributed via an off-domain Google Drive link, so no official SVG is served from synthflow.ai.

controlling_quote: Use of the Cloudflare logos (other than the use of Web Badges described below) requires our written permission.
note: The only unlicensed logo-form use is the web badge, and it is conditioned on the site actually being protected and accelerated by Cloudflare — a customer relationship AgenID does not have. Cloudflare does publish approved wording for exactly what AgenID needs to say, in word-mark form only: 'runs on,' 'for use with,' 'for,' or 'compatible with.' The press-kit archive contains JPG and PNG only; no SVG is offered.

controlling_quote: Any such use should be in plain text only (no logos).
note: The quoted sentence is from the Fair Use section — AWS's own safe harbour for unaffiliated third parties is explicitly text-only. Section 9 separately bars altering logo images 'including but not limited to changing the proportion, color, or font,' and Section 3(d) requires prior written permission for anything outside the customer/partner licences. The Architecture Icons are a separate and narrower grant, running to 'customers and partners' for architecture diagrams and technical material, and they do not include the AWS corporate logo. AWS does publish the approved relational phrases for text use, among them 'compatible with' and 'works with'.

controlling_quote: Don't use the Google logo in marketing materials for a business or to imply endorsement from Google.
note: The Google Cloud icons page carries no licence grant of any kind — neither the page nor its 34-page PDF contains terms of use, and the PDF is marked 'Google Cloud Proprietary & Confidential.' Absent a grant there, Google's general brand rules govern, and they permit logo use to refer to Google only 'so long as it's not being used for marketing or business purposes.'

controlling_quote: However, our logos, app and product icons, illustrations, photographs, videos, and designs can never be used without an express license.
note: The most explicit of the sixteen on the specific treatment this sprint proposed: Microsoft's third-party logo guidance lists 'Don't make the logo a single color' as a common error outright. Microsoft Azure is named by name among the brand assets requiring authorization. The Azure architecture icons carry their own closed licence — 'architectural diagrams, training materials, or documentation' — which an ecosystem graphic is none of.

controlling_quote: However, Twilio restricts use of the Twilio corporate logo, and you may not use it without our express written permission.
note: Twilio pre-empts the usual rationalisation in terms worth keeping: 'Affiliation with Twilio or Twilio programs does not imply the right to use the Twilio logo.' If a formal partner gets no logo rights from the partnership alone, a party documenting technical compatibility certainly gets none. The 'Powered by Twilio' badge is the only self-serve mark and is limited to customers in good standing; there is no 'Built on Twilio' badge, and creating one would violate the bar on making your own. Twilio is also the only provider of the sixteen requiring an attribution notice where its marks are used.

controlling_quote: Use our Marks only on the portion of your website or application that directly relates to our services (such as on a checkout page using our payment processing services).
note: The freely downloadable SVG kit is the trap here: the newsroom page states plainly that all brand elements remain subject to the Marks Usage Agreement, whose terms are addressed to Stripe Users and scoped to the part of a site that directly relates to Stripe's services. A marketing ecosystem graphic is not that portion. Colour is closed separately — 'Do not use any other color for the wordmark.' 'Powered by Stripe' is for businesses who use Stripe, on their checkout pages.

controlling_quote: Our logo is a core element of our brand. We ask that you use it in a consistent manner and do not rotate, alter, or add colors and effects to our wordmark.
note: Held for review by the brief and excluded on independent grounds: no documented mechanism was found for carrying an agenid:<ULID> through Coinbase, so it does not belong in the ecosystem registry on technical merit either — which is why registry_id is null. Its brand terms are also the broadest of the sixteen, asking third parties to promise not to use Coinbase marks for personal or commercial use. The published asset archive has not been refreshed since 2021.
